in_text_mentions: lmost complete loss of his eyebrows was noticed. Dermatological examination showed a few hairs on the lateral sides, while there were just black dots and some broken hairs on the remaining part of the eyebrows (Figure 1). Trichoscopic examination revealed various findings, namely broken hairs at different lengths, coiled hairs, hook hairs, short hairs with trichoptilosis, V-sign, flame hairs, tulip hairs, black dots, and a few yellow dots (Figure 2, A and B). After we took a careful history, he reported that he had been pulling out his eyebrow hairs during stressful times for the past 4 years.

panels.figure_caption: Trichotillomania lesions on vertex of scalp.
in_text_mentions: rmatological survey, these lesions were located on the easily approachable aspect of bilateral upper limbs and dorsum of bilateral feet (Figures 2 and 3), with sparing of the usually covered and unapproachable areas of limbs, trunk, and genitalia. Also, there was an area of short, irregular, broken, and distorted hair on the scalp, mainly over the vertex, suggesting hair pulling and plucking (Figure 4), whereas eyebrows, eyelashes, pubic hair, and other body hair were spared. This characteristic distribution of the lesions displayed signs of self-inflicted wounds rather than physical violence.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left photo with yellow circle caption as 'Erosion of the entire crown of the scalp to expose the skull' in article titled 'Severe Trichotillomania' with in-text suspicion of self-injury/repetitive behavior; shows large irregular patchy alopecia with broken hairs around erosive denuded scalp. B: Right photo with blue circle caption as 'Another lesion was noted behind the right ear' in severe trichotillomania case with self-injury; shows ulcerated lesion with surrounding irregular broken hair/alopecia.
panels.attribution_text: Check et al. Severe Trichotillomania: An Unusual Trigger of Recurrent Diabetic Ketoacidosis.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.21384. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Erosion of the entire crown of the scalp to expose the skull (yellow circle). Another lesion was noted behind the right ear (blue circle).
in_text_mentions: The initial differential diagnosis of a young type 1 diabetic with recurrent DKA, microcytic anemia, persistent granulomatous non-healing lesions, and recurrent diarrhea was broad and concerning for pyoderma gangrenosum in addition to infectious causes of ulcerative lesions, malignancy, and various forms of vasculitis. While reviewing the photographs, the very smooth borders of the lesions in addition to the lesions being at various stages of healing raised suspicion of the possibility of self-injury and repetitive behavior. Images of the skin lesions are shown in Figures 1-2.
